description: How data is stored, processed, streamed and served across clusters, from MapReduce to feature stores. Students write dataflow jobs, run cluster experiments in the cloud console, tune queries on the database engine and benchmark systems with proper methodology.
modelledOn: Karau, Konwinski, Wendell and Zaharia, Learning Spark
The original MapReduce and Google File System research papers
outcomes: Express batch analytics as MapReduce and dataflow jobs and reason about shuffle cost, skew and fault recovery.
Choose file formats, storage engines and partitioning schemes for a given access pattern.
Build stream processing pipelines with correct windowing, state and delivery semantics.
Explain cluster resource management, data-parallel training and feature store design for machine learning platforms.
Design and run a sound benchmark and use scalability laws and cost models to justify an architecture.

units.title: MapReduce and dataflow engines
topics: The MapReduce model: map, shuffle, sort and reduce; combiners
Fault tolerance: task re-execution, stragglers and speculative execution
Algorithms in MapReduce: word count, inverted index, reduce-side and map-side joins
Dataflow DAG engines: resilient datasets, lineage and lazy evaluation
Spark-style transformations: narrow and wide dependencies, partitioning and shuffle cost
Data skew: salting, broadcast joins and adaptive partitioning

units.title: Distributed file systems and column stores
topics: Distributed file system design: name node, blocks, replication and rack awareness
Object stores versus distributed file systems
File formats: row versus columnar, Parquet-style encodings (dictionary, run-length), predicate pushdown
Log-structured merge trees and wide-column stores
Partitioning, sharding and bloom filters
Table formats and the lakehouse: snapshots, ACID on object storage

units.title: Stream processing and message queues
topics: Log-based message queues: partitions, offsets, consumer groups and retention
Delivery semantics: at-most-once, at-least-once and exactly-once with idempotence
Event time, processing time, windows and watermarks
Stateful stream processing and checkpoints
Stream joins and change data capture
Backpressure, throughput and latency trade-offs
Case study: real-time fraud scoring on a mobile money transaction stream

units.title: Cluster resource managers
topics: Two-level resource managers and application masters
Running data jobs on container orchestrators
Fair, capacity and dominant-resource schedulers
Data locality and gang scheduling
Multi-tenancy: quotas, queues and preemption

units.title: Feature stores and ML training platforms
topics: The ML pipeline from raw data to a deployed model
Feature stores: offline and online stores, point-in-time correctness
Data-parallel training: parameter servers, ring all-reduce and gradient synchronisation
Model and pipeline parallelism and memory limits
Experiment tracking, hyperparameter search and reproducibility
Training-serving skew and how to prevent it

units.title: Serving, caching and cost control
topics: Online serving: latency budgets, batching and tail latency
Caching layers: in-memory stores, invalidation strategies and hit-rate modelling
Model serving rollouts: shadow, canary and rollback
Cost models for storage, compute and network; spot capacity and autoscaling
Query acceleration: materialised views, pre-aggregation and indexing
Capacity planning from growth forecasts

units.title: Benchmarking big data workloads
topics: Workload characterisation: access patterns, skew and arrival rates
Benchmark suites: TPC-H style analytics and YCSB-style key-value workloads
Methodology: warm-up, repetitions, percentiles and confidence intervals
Scalability analysis: speedup, strong and weak scaling, Amdahl's law and the universal scalability law
Profiling bottlenecks and reporting results honestly

units.title: End-to-end pipeline project
topics: Designing an ingest-to-serve pipeline for a national dataset
Failure injection and recovery testing
Comparative evaluation of two design alternatives
Project report and architecture defence

schedule.title: MapReduce model and algorithms
schedule.exercise: Write the map and reduce functions for an inverted index over 1,000 news articles, describe what moves across the network, and show how a combiner reduces it.

tasks.title: Implement word count with map, shuffle and reduce functions in code and run it on a 10-line text to check the counts
Implement a reduce-side join of orders and customers, then rewrite it as a map-side join with a broadcast table and compare data moved
Run a job on a small cluster, kill one worker mid-run and slow another, and show how task re-execution and speculation restore progress

schedule.title: Dataflow engines and skew
schedule.exercise: Mark each step of a Spark-style job as a narrow or wide dependency, count the shuffles, and propose a fix for a join where one key holds 60 percent of rows.

tasks.title: Write a transformation chain in a notebook, print its lineage, and mark which steps trigger a shuffle
Recompute a lost partition from lineage by deleting one cached partition and show the result is identical after recomputation
Generate a skewed key distribution, time a join, then apply key salting and a broadcast join and compare the runtime of each

schedule.title: Distributed storage and file formats
schedule.exercise: Compute the storage and read cost of a 1 TB table in row and columnar formats when a query touches 3 of 40 columns, and explain how dictionary and run-length encoding shrink it.

tasks.title: Write a large file to a distributed store, list its blocks and replicas by node and rack, and record the placement
Store the same table as CSV and in a columnar format, query three columns, and compare file size and scan time
Compare listing and reading 10,000 small files on an object store against one large file and explain the cost per request

schedule.title: LSM trees, partitioning and lakehouse tables
schedule.exercise: Trace writes through a memtable, flushes and compactions in an LSM tree, and choose a partition key for a call-detail table to avoid hot partitions.

tasks.title: Step through inserts into a memtable, flush to sorted files, and compaction, and record the files present after each step
Implement a bloom filter, load 10,000 keys, and measure false positive rate against bit-array size and number of hash functions
Partition a transactions table by date and by region, run the same query on both layouts, and compare the rows scanned

schedule.title: Message logs, delivery semantics and event time
schedule.exercise: Explain how a duplicate message arises under at-least-once delivery and design an idempotent consumer, then compute tumbling and sliding window counts for a late-arriving event.

tasks.title: Publish 100 messages to a partitioned log, read them with two consumers in a group, and show which partition each reads
Crash a consumer before it commits an offset, observe duplicates, then make processing idempotent so the final count is exact
Compute tumbling window counts on out-of-order events with a watermark and measure how many late events are dropped for three lateness bounds

schedule.title: Stateful streams, joins and backpressure
schedule.exercise: Design a fraud-scoring stream for mobile money that joins each transfer with a customer profile, keeps per-account state, and meets a 200 ms latency target at a given load.

tasks.title: Keep a running per-account total in a stream job, take a checkpoint, restart it, and confirm the totals continue unchanged
Join a transaction stream with a slowly changing customer table using a change feed, and show the join reflects an update
Scale a fraud-scoring stream job under rising load, observe backpressure, and tune partitions and parallelism to keep latency under 200 ms

schedule.title: Cluster resource management
schedule.exercise: Allocate a 100-core cluster among three teams with capacity queues, simulate a burst job, and explain when preemption is justified and what it costs.

tasks.title: Submit three jobs to a shared cluster and record which containers each got on which nodes and how long they waited
Simulate FIFO, fair and capacity scheduling on a mixed job trace and compare mean waiting time and utilisation
Add data locality to a scheduler simulation, measure the fraction of local tasks versus waiting delay, and tune the delay parameter

schedule.title: ML pipelines, feature stores and data-parallel training
schedule.exercise: Show how joining features without point-in-time logic leaks the future into training, and compute the communication volume of parameter-server versus ring all-reduce for 8 workers.

tasks.title: Run a pipeline of ingest, feature creation, training and evaluation on a small dataset and record the output of each stage
Build features with a point-in-time join and again with a naive join, and show the inflated accuracy that leakage causes
Step through ring all-reduce for 4 workers, count the messages and bytes per step, and compare with a central parameter server

schedule.title: Large models, experiments and skew
schedule.exercise: Decide whether a model that does not fit one GPU needs model or pipeline parallelism, set up an experiment log for a hyperparameter search, and find a training-serving skew in a given pipeline.

tasks.title: Log parameters, metrics and the data version for five training runs and use the log to reproduce the best run exactly
Run random search and grid search on the same budget and compare the best validation score each finds
Compare feature values computed in the training pipeline and the online service for 100 rows, find the mismatch, and fix its cause

schedule.title: Serving latency, caching and rollouts
schedule.exercise: Model the hit rate of an LRU cache for a Zipf-distributed request pattern, compute the mean latency saved, and plan a canary rollout with rollback criteria for a new model version.

tasks.title: Add an LRU cache in front of a slow lookup function, replay 1,000 requests, and report hit rate and mean latency
Increase request rate on a model server with and without batching, and compare median and 99th percentile latency
Route 5 percent of traffic to a new model version, compare error and latency with the old, and roll back when the rule is breached

schedule.title: Cost, query acceleration and capacity planning
schedule.exercise: Estimate the monthly bill for a 50 TB analytics platform under on-demand and spot compute, and show how a materialised summary table changes cost and query time.

tasks.title: Estimate monthly storage, compute and network cost for a described pipeline with the pricing calculator and list the biggest line item
Create a pre-aggregated summary table for a daily revenue query, compare the query plans and timings before and after
Fit a growth curve to 18 months of data volume, project capacity for 24 months ahead, and decide when to add nodes

schedule.title: Benchmark design and scalability analysis
schedule.exercise: Write a benchmark plan for comparing two storage engines under a read-heavy skewed workload, with warm-up, repetitions and the statistics you will report.

tasks.title: Run a benchmark ten times, discard the warm-up runs, and report median, 95th percentile and a confidence interval
Run a set of analytic queries at two data sizes on the database engine and report the time for each query with the plan
Fit Amdahl's law and the universal scalability law to measured speedups for 1 to 32 workers and explain where each model fails

schedule.title: Pipeline project and defence
schedule.exercise: Present a pipeline for ingesting national health facility reports, with storage layout, processing, serving, failure handling and measured results for two design options.

tasks.title: Draw an ingest-to-serve pipeline for facility reports labelling storage formats, processing stages, queues and the serving layer
Kill a processing node and a message broker in your pipeline in turn, record what is lost or delayed, and fix the gaps
Run two designs for the same pipeline under the same load and report throughput, latency and cost per million records
